description: Execute a command on the user’s paired computer in the selected local folder and return stdout, stderr and exit status. Check the current local-workspace-capabilities context for Shell permission. Each call uses a fresh shell.

contexts.offline: Local workspace connection: offline. File and terminal operations are unavailable until the user reconnects this folder in the desktop app or local companion.
contexts.disabled: Local workspace connection: online. Shell permission: disabled. File tools remain available. To run commands, the user must reconnect with Shell enabled; the command-line companion requires --allow-shell. Desktop control permission: disabled, so computer_screenshot and computer_use are not available. To grant it the user turns on desktop control for this folder in the desktop app, or reconnects the command-line companion with --allow-desktop, and then starts a new conversation: these two tools are selected when a conversation begins, unlike the Shell permission, which this line reports live.
contexts.enabled: Local workspace connection: online. Shell permission: enabled. The bash tool runs Bash in the selected local folder as the current operating-system user. Terminal operations are already authorized; no --allow-shell startup step is needed for this connection. Each call starts a fresh shell. Operating-system permissions still apply; this does not grant administrator or root privileges. Desktop control permission: disabled, so computer_screenshot and computer_use are not available. To grant it the user turns on desktop control for this folder in the desktop app, or reconnects the command-line companion with --allow-desktop, and then starts a new conversation: these two tools are selected when a conversation begins, unlike the Shell permission, which this line reports live.

Operating-system permissions still apply; this does not grant administrator or root privileges. Desktop control permission: disabled, so computer_screenshot and computer_use are not available. To grant it the user turns on desktop control for this folder in the desktop app, or reconnects the command-line companion with --allow-desktop, and then starts a new conversation: these two tools are selected when a conversation begins, unlike the Shell permission, which this line reports live.
contexts.desktopEnabled: Local workspace connection: online. Shell permission: enabled. The bash tool runs Bash in the selected local folder as the current operating-system user. Terminal operations are already authorized; no --allow-shell startup step is needed for this connection. Each call starts a fresh shell. Operating-system permissions still apply; this does not grant administrator or root privileges. Desktop control permission: enabled. computer_screenshot captures that computer’s screen and computer_use drives its mouse and keyboard as the current operating-system user. Coordinates are measured on the returned screenshot, never on the physical display.
